sanskrit: baladarpasamutsiktas takṣakaḥ pannagādhamaḥ akāryaṃ kṛtavān pāpo yo 'daśat pitaraṃ tava
english: Takṣaka, the vilest of serpents, swollen with the arrogance of power, acted wickedly — that sinful one who bit your father.

sanskrit: rājarṣivaṃśagoptāram amarapratimaḥ nṛpam jaghāna kāśyapaṃ caiva nyavartayata pāpakṛt
english: That evil-doer slew the king who was equal to the immortals and guardian of the royal-seer lineage, and also turned back Kaśyapa.

sanskrit: dagdhum arhasi taṃ pāpaṃ jvalite havyavāhane sarpasatre mahārāja tvayi tad dhi vidhīyate
english: You should burn that sinner in the blazing fire of the oblation-carrier, O great king — for that very purpose is the serpent sacrifice ordained for you.

sanskrit: evaṃ pituś cāpacitiṃ gatavāṃs tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi mama priyaṃ ca sumahat kṛtaṃ rājan bhaviṣyati
english: In this way you shall have fully avenged your father, O king, and you will have done something exceedingly dear to me.

sanskrit: karmaṇaḥ pṛthivīpāla mama yena durātmanā vighnaḥ kṛto mahārāja gurvarthaṃ carato 'nagha
english: O protector of the earth, great king, O sinless one — an obstacle was made to my task by that evil-souled one, while I was performing my duty toward my teacher.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu nṛpatis takṣakasya cukopa ha uttaṅkavākyahaviṣā dīpto 'gnir haviṣā yathā
english: Having heard this, the king became furious at Takṣaka — kindled by the oblation of Uttaṅka's words as fire is kindled by clarified butter.

sanskrit: apṛcchac ca tadā rājā mantriṇaḥ svān suduḥkhitaḥ uttaṅkasyaiva sāṃnidhye pituḥ svargagatiṃ prati
english: Deeply grieved, the king then asked his ministers — even in the very presence of Uttaṅka — concerning his father's passage to heaven.

sanskrit: tadaiva hi sa rājendro duḥkhaśokāpluto 'bhavat yadaiva pitaraṃ vṛttam uttaṅkād aśṛṇot tadā
english: That lord of kings was overwhelmed with grief and sorrow at that very moment when he heard from Uttaṅka of his father's fate.

sanskrit: lomaharṣaṇaputra ugraśravāḥ sūtaḥ paurāṇiko naimiṣāraṇye śaunakasya kulapater dvādaśavārṣike satre ṛṣīn abhyāgatān upatasthe
english: Ugraśravās, the son of Lomaharṣaṇa, a sūta skilled in the Purāṇas, attended upon the seers who had come together at the twelve-year sacrifice of the householder Śaunaka in the Naimiṣa forest.

sanskrit: paurāṇikaḥ purāṇe kṛtaśramaḥ sa tān kṛtāñjalir uvāca kiṃ bhavantaḥ śrotum icchanti kim ahaṃ bruvāṇīti
english: That one well-versed in the Purāṇas, experienced in purāṇic lore, addressed them with joined palms: "What do you wish to hear? What shall I recite?"

sanskrit: tam ṛṣaya ūcuḥ paramaṃ lomaharṣaṇe prakṣyāmas tvāṃ vakṣyasi ca naḥ śuśrūṣatāṃ kathāyogam tad bhagavāṃs tu tāvac chaunako 'gniśaraṇam adhyāste
english: The seers said: "O Lomaharṣaṇa, we shall ask you the highest matter, and you shall narrate to us who are eager to listen the connected narrative — but first, the venerable Śaunaka is presiding over the fire-sanctuary."

sanskrit: yo 'sau divyāḥ kathā veda devatāsurasaṃkathāḥ manuṣyoragagandharvakathā veda ca sarvaśaḥ
english: He knows the divine stories, the tales of gods and demons, the stories of men, serpents, and gandharvas — he knows them all in every detail.

sanskrit: sa cāpy asmin makhe saute vidvān kulapatir dvijaḥ dakṣo dhṛtavrato dhīmāñ śāstre cāraṇyake guruḥ
english: And he, O sūta, is the learned head of the assembly, a brahmin, capable, firm in vows, wise, and a master in both the śāstra and the āraṇyaka.

sanskrit: satyavādī śamaparas tapasvī niyatavrataḥ sarveṣām eva no mānyaḥ sa tāvat pratipālyatām
english: He is a speaker of truth, devoted to tranquility, an ascetic, steadfast in his vows — he is deserving of reverence from all of us; let him be waited upon first.

sanskrit: tasminn adhyāsati gurāv āsanaṃ paramārcitam tato vakṣyasi yat tvāṃ sa prakṣyati dvijasattamaḥ
english: When that teacher is seated on his most honored seat, then you shall narrate whatever that best of twice-born men asks of you.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca evam astu gurau tasminn upaviṣṭe mahātmani tena pṛṣṭaḥ kathāḥ puṇyā vakṣyāmi vividhāśrayāḥ
english: The sūta said: "So be it — when that great-souled teacher is seated and has asked me, I shall narrate the sacred stories that touch upon various subjects."

sanskrit: so 'tha viprarṣabhaḥ kāryaṃ kṛtvā sarvaṃ yathākramam devān vāgbhiḥ pitṝn adbhis tarpayitvājagāma ha
english: That foremost brahmin then, having completed all his duties in proper order, having satisfied the gods with hymns and the ancestors with water, arrived there.

sanskrit: yatra brahmarṣayaḥ siddhās ta āsīnā yatavratāḥ yajñāyatanam āśritya sūtaputrapuraḥsarāḥ
english: There the accomplished brahmin-seers were seated, firm in their vows, gathered at the sacrificial enclosure, with the sūta's son at their fore.

sanskrit: ṛtvikṣv atha sadasyeṣu sa vai gṛhapatis tataḥ upaviṣṭeṣūpaviṣṭaḥ śaunako 'thābravīd idam
english: When the officiating priests and the assembly members had taken their seats, the householder Śaunaka seated himself and then spoke thus.

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca purāṇam akhilaṃ tāta pitā te 'dhītavān purā kaccit tvam api tat sarvam adhīṣe lomaharṣaṇe
english: Śaunaka said: "My dear son, your father formerly studied the entire Purāṇa — have you too studied all of that, O Lomaharṣaṇa?"

sanskrit: purāṇe hi kathā divyā ādivaṃśāś ca dhīmatām kathyante tāḥ purāsmābhiḥ śrutāḥ pūrvaṃ pitus tava
english: "For in the Purāṇa are told divine stories and the primordial lineages of the wise — those were formerly heard by us from your father."

sanskrit: tatra vaṃśam ahaṃ pūrvaṃ śrotum icchāmi bhārgavam kathayasva kathām etāṃ kalyāḥ sma śravaṇe tava
english: "Among those, I wish first to hear the lineage of Bhṛgu — narrate that story; we are fit and ready to hear from you."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca yad adhītaṃ purā samyag dvijaśreṣṭha mahātmabhiḥ vaiśaṃpāyanaviprādyais taiś cāpi kathitaṃ purā
english: The sūta said: "What was formerly studied thoroughly by the great-souled ones headed by the brahmin Vaiśaṃpāyana, and what was formerly narrated by them —

sanskrit: yad adhītaṃ ca pitrā me samyak caiva tato mayā tat tāvac chṛṇu yo devaiḥ sendraiḥ sāgnimarudgaṇaiḥ pūjitaḥ pravaro vaṃśo bhṛgūṇāṃ bhṛgunandana
english: "What was studied by my father and in turn by me in full — hear first that lineage which is honored by the gods together with Indra, Agni, and the Marut hosts: the foremost lineage of the Bhṛgus, O delight of Bhṛgu."

sanskrit: imaṃ vaṃśam ahaṃ brahman bhārgavaṃ te mahāmune nigadāmi kathāyuktaṃ purāṇāśrayasaṃyutam
english: "O brahmin, O great sage, I shall recite for you this lineage of Bhārgava accompanied by its narrative and grounded in purāṇic tradition."

sanskrit: bhṛgoḥ sudayitaḥ putraś cyavano nāma bhārgavaḥ cyavanasyāpi dāyādaḥ pramatir nāma dhārmikaḥ pramater apy abhūt putro ghṛtācyāṃ rurur ity uta
english: The deeply beloved son of Bhṛgu was Cyavana of the Bhārgava line; Cyavana's heir was the righteous one named Pramati; and from Pramati was born a son in Ghṛtācī named Ruru.

sanskrit: ruror api suto jajñe śunako vedapāragaḥ pramadvarāyāṃ dharmātmā tava pūrvapitāmahāt
english: From Ruru too was born a son who had crossed to the further shore of the Vedas — the righteous-souled Śunaka, born of Pramadvarā — your own great-grandfather.

sanskrit: tapasvī ca yaśasvī ca śrutavān brahmavittamaḥ dharmiṣṭhaḥ satyavādī ca niyato niyatendriyaḥ
english: He was an ascetic, illustrious, learned, the foremost knower of Brahman, most righteous, a speaker of truth, disciplined, with controlled senses.

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca sūtaputra yathā tasya bhārgavasya mahātmanaḥ cyavanatvaṃ parikhyātaṃ tan mamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ
english: Śaunaka said: "O son of the sūta, how the name 'Cyavana' became renowned for that great-souled Bhārgava — tell me that, as I ask."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca bhṛgoḥ sudayitā bhāryā pulomety abhiviśrutā tasyāṃ garbhaḥ samabhavad bhṛgor vīryasamudbhavaḥ
english: The sūta said: "The dearly beloved wife of Bhṛgu was renowned as Pulomā; in her a child was conceived, born of Bhṛgu's seed."

sanskrit: tasmin garbhe saṃbhṛte 'tha pulomāyāṃ bhṛgūdvaha samaye samaśīlinyāṃ dharmapatnyāṃ yaśasvinaḥ
english: "While that embryo was growing in Pulomā, O foremost of the Bhṛgu line — at that time, in the illustrious one's righteous wife who shared his disposition —"

sanskrit: abhiṣekāya niṣkrānte bhṛgau dharmabhṛtāṃ vare āśramaṃ tasya rakṣo 'tha pulomābhyājagāma ha
english: "When Bhṛgu, the foremost of the upholders of dharma, had gone out to bathe, a rakṣasa came to his hermitage and approached Pulomā."

sanskrit: taṃ praviśyāśramaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhṛgor bhāryām aninditām hṛcchayena samāviṣṭo vicetāḥ samapadyata
english: "Entering the hermitage and seeing the blameless wife of Bhṛgu, he was seized by desire and became bewildered, losing his senses."

sanskrit: abhyāgataṃ tu tad rakṣaḥ pulomā cārudarśanā nyamantrayata vanyena phalamūlādinā tadā
english: "The beautiful-looking Pulomā then received that rakṣasa as a guest with forest offerings of fruits, roots, and the like."

sanskrit: tāṃ tu rakṣas tato brahman hṛcchayenābhipīḍitam dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭam abhūt tatra jihīrṣus tām aninditām
english: "But that rakṣasa, O brahmin, tormented by desire upon seeing her, rejoiced there, wishing to abduct that blameless woman."

sanskrit: athāgniśaraṇe 'paśyaj jvalitaṃ jātavedasam tam apṛcchat tato rakṣaḥ pāvakaṃ jvalitaṃ tadā
english: "Then he saw Jātavedas blazing in the fire-shrine; the rakṣasa then asked the blazing purifier Fire —"

sanskrit: śaṃsa me kasya bhāryeyam agne pṛṣṭa ṛtena vai satyas tvam asi satyaṃ me vada pāvaka pṛcchate
english: "'Tell me, O Agni, whose wife is this? You have been truly asked — you are Truth itself; speak truth to me who asks, O purifier.'"

sanskrit: mayā hīyaṃ pūrvavṛtā bhāryārthe varavarṇinī paścāt tv imāṃ pitā prādād bhṛgave 'nṛtakāriṇe
english: "'This fair-complexioned woman was first chosen by me for the purpose of marriage, yet afterward her father gave her to Bhṛgu, that doer of untruth.'"

sanskrit: seyaṃ yadi varārohā bhṛgor bhāryā rahogatā tathā satyaṃ samākhyāhi jihīrṣāmy āśramād imām
english: "'If this fine-hipped woman is indeed Bhṛgu's wife who has come here alone, then tell me truly — I wish to take her away from this hermitage.'"

sanskrit: manyur hi hṛdayaṃ me 'dya pradahann iva tiṣṭhati matpurvabhāryāṃ yad imāṃ bhṛguḥ prāpa sumadhyamām
english: "'For rage burns as though scorching my heart today, since Bhṛgu took her — this slender-waisted one who was formerly my wife.'"

sanskrit: tad rakṣa evam āmantrya jvalitaṃ jātavedasam śaṅkamāno bhṛgor bhāryāṃ punaḥ punar apṛcchata
english: "Having thus addressed the blazing Jātavedas, the rakṣasa, uncertain about Bhṛgu's wife, asked again and again."

sanskrit: tvam agne sarvabhūtānām antaś carasi nityadā sākṣivat puṇyapāpeṣu satyaṃ brūhi kave vacaḥ
english: "'You, O Agni, dwell eternally within all beings as a witness to their virtuous and sinful deeds — speak truthfully, O wise one; utter words of truth.'"

sanskrit: matpūrvabhāryāpahṛtā bhṛguṇānṛtakāriṇā seyaṃ yadi tathā me tvaṃ satyam ākhyātum arhasi
english: "'If this is she — my former wife, taken by Bhṛgu that doer of untruth — then you ought to tell me truly.'"

sanskrit: śrutvā tvatto bhṛgor bhāryāṃ hariṣyāmy aham āśramāt jātavedaḥ paśyatas te vada satyāṃ giraṃ mama
english: "'Having heard from you that she is Bhṛgu's wife, I shall carry her away from this hermitage — O Jātavedas, even as you look on, speak my true words to me.'"

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā saptārcir duḥkhito bhṛśam bhīto 'nṛtāc ca śāpāc ca bhṛgor ity abravīc chanaiḥ
english: "Hearing those words of his, the seven-flamed Fire was deeply troubled, fearful both of falsehood and of Bhṛgu's curse, and spoke softly —"

sanskrit: agner atha vacaḥ śrutvā tad rakṣaḥ prajahāra tām brahman varāharūpeṇa manomārutaraṃhasā
english: The sūta said: "Then, O brahmin, having heard the words of Agni, that rakṣasa seized her, taking the form of a boar and swift as mind and wind."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa garbho nivasan kukṣau bhṛgukulodvaha roṣān mātuś cyutaḥ kukṣeś cyavanas tena so 'bhavat
english: "Then that child dwelling in the womb — O foremost of the Bhṛgu line — fell from his mother's womb in anger, and by that falling he became known as Cyavana."

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā mātur udarāc cyutam ādityavarcasam tad rakṣo bhasmasād bhūtaṃ papāta parimucya tām
english: "Seeing him, blazing with the radiance of the sun, fallen from his mother's womb, that rakṣasa was reduced to ashes and fell, releasing her."

sanskrit: sā tam ādāya suśroṇī sasāra bhṛgunandanam cyavanaṃ bhārgavaṃ brahman pulomā duḥkhamūrcchitā
english: "Taking him, the beautiful-hipped Pulomā — the delight of Bhṛgu — O brahmin, walked on with Cyavana of the Bhārgava line, faint with sorrow."

sanskrit: tāṃ dadarśa svayaṃ brahmā sarvalokapitāmahaḥ rudatīṃ bāṣpapūrṇākṣīṃ bhṛgor bhāryām aninditām sāntvayām āsa bhagavān vadhūṃ brahmā pitāmahaḥ
english: "Brahmā himself, the grandfather of all worlds, saw her — Bhṛgu's blameless wife weeping, her eyes filled with tears — and the venerable grandfather Brahmā comforted that daughter-in-law."

sanskrit: aśrubindūdbhavā tasyāḥ prāvartata mahānadī anuvartatī sṛtiṃ tasyā bhṛgoḥ patnyā yaśasvinaḥ
english: "From the drops of her tears a great river flowed forth, following the path of that illustrious wife of Bhṛgu as she walked."

sanskrit: tasyā mārgaṃ sṛtavatīṃ dṛṣṭvā tu saritaṃ tadā nāma tasyās tadā nadyāś cakre lokapitāmahaḥ vadhūsareti bhagavāṃś cyavanasyāśramaṃ prati
english: "Seeing that river flowing along her path, the grandfather of the worlds then gave that river its name — calling it Vadhūsarā — as it flowed toward Cyavana's hermitage."

sanskrit: sa evaṃ cyavano jajñe bhṛgoḥ putraḥ pratāpavān taṃ dadarśa pitā tatra cyavanaṃ tāṃ ca bhāminīm
english: "In this way the mighty Cyavana was born as the son of Bhṛgu; the father saw Cyavana there, and also that illustrious woman."

sanskrit: sa pulomāṃ tato bhāryāṃ papraccha kupito bhṛguḥ kenāsi rakṣase tasmai kathiteha jihīrṣave na hi tvāṃ veda tad rakṣo madbhāryāṃ cāruhāsinīm
english: "Then the enraged Bhṛgu asked his wife Pulomā: 'By whom were you here pointed out to that rakṣasa who wished to abduct you? For that rakṣasa did not know you, my fair-smiling wife.'"

sanskrit: tat tvam ākhyāhi taṃ hy adya śaptum icchāmy ahaṃ ruṣā bibheti ko na śāpān me kasya cāyaṃ vyatikramaḥ
english: "'Tell me that — for I wish today to curse him in my anger. Who does not fear my curse? Whose transgression is this?'"

sanskrit: pulomovāca agninā bhagavaṃs tasmai rakṣase 'haṃ niveditā tato mām anayad rakṣaḥ krośantīṃ kurarīm iva
english: "Pulomā said: 'It was by Agni, O venerable one, that I was disclosed to that rakṣasa; thereupon the rakṣasa carried me off even as I cried out like an osprey.'"

sanskrit: sāhaṃ tava sutasyāsya tejasā parimokṣitā bhasmībhūtaṃ ca tad rakṣo mām utsṛjya papāta vai
english: "'I was freed by the radiance of this your son; that rakṣasa, reduced to ashes, fell releasing me.'"

sanskrit: sūta uvāca iti śrutvā pulomāyā bhṛguḥ paramamanyumān śaśāpāgnim abhikruddhaḥ sarvabhakṣo bhaviṣyasi
english: The sūta said: "Having heard this from Pulomā, Bhṛgu was seized with utmost fury and, thoroughly enraged, cursed Agni: 'You shall become the eater of all things!'"

sanskrit: sūta uvāca śaptas tu bhṛguṇā vahniḥ kruddho vākyam athābravīt kim idaṃ sāhasaṃ brahman kṛtavān asi sāṃpratam
english: The sūta said: "Cursed by Bhṛgu, the fire became angry and spoke: 'What rash deed have you done now, O brahmin?'"

sanskrit: dharme prayatamānasya satyaṃ ca vadataḥ samam pṛṣṭo yad abruvaṃ satyaṃ vyabhicāro 'tra ko mama
english: "'For one striving in dharma, speaking truth impartially, when asked, I spoke truth — what transgression is mine in this?'"

sanskrit: pṛṣṭo hi sākṣī yaḥ sākṣyaṃ jānamāno 'nyathā vadet sa pūrvān ātmanaḥ sapta kule hanyāt tathā parān
english: "'For a witness who, when asked, knowingly gives false testimony destroys seven of his own ancestors as well as seven in the opposing family.'"

sanskrit: yaś ca kāryārthatattvajño jānamāno na bhāṣate so 'pi tenaiva pāpena lipyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: "'And one who knows the truth of a matter yet does not speak when knowing — he too is tainted by that very sin; of this there is no doubt.'"

sanskrit: śakto 'ham api śaptuṃ tvāṃ mānyās tu brāhmaṇā mama jānato 'pi ca te vyaktaṃ kathayiṣye nibodha tat
english: "'I too am capable of cursing you, yet brahmins are to be honored by me — even though knowing, I shall explain clearly to you; understand this.'"

sanskrit: yogena bahudhātmānaṃ kṛtvā tiṣṭhāmi mūrtiṣu agnihotreṣu satreṣu kriyāsv atha makheṣu ca
english: "'By my power, dividing myself manifold, I dwell in many forms — in the agnihotras, in the sattras, in the ritual acts, and in the sacrifices.'"

sanskrit: vedoktena vidhānena mayi yad dhūyate haviḥ devatāḥ pitaraś caiva tena tṛptā bhavanti vai
english: "'Whatever oblation is offered into me according to the ordinance prescribed by the Vedas — by that the gods and ancestors become satisfied.'"

sanskrit: āpo devagaṇāḥ sarve āpaḥ pitṛgaṇās tathā darśaś ca paurṇamāsaś ca devānāṃ pitṛbhiḥ saha
english: "'Water constitutes all the hosts of gods; water likewise constitutes the hosts of ancestors; the new-moon and full-moon rites belong to gods together with ancestors.'"

sanskrit: devatāḥ pitaras tasmāt pitaraś cāpi devatāḥ ekībhūtāś ca pūjyante pṛthaktvena ca parvasu
english: "'Therefore the gods are the ancestors and the ancestors too are gods; they are worshipped as one and also separately at the sacred occasions.'"

sanskrit: devatāḥ pitaraś caiva juhvate mayi yat sadā tridaśānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca mukham evam ahaṃ smṛtaḥ
english: "'Whatever the gods and ancestors constantly offer into me — thus I am known as the mouth of the thirty gods and of the ancestors.'"

sanskrit: amāvāsyāṃ ca pitaraḥ paurṇamāsyāṃ ca devatāḥ manmukhenaiva hūyante bhuñjate ca hutaṃ haviḥ sarvabhakṣaḥ kathaṃ teṣāṃ bhaviṣyāmi mukhaṃ tv aham
english: "'On the new-moon day the ancestors, and on the full-moon day the gods, are invoked through my mouth alone and consume the offered oblation — how then shall I become the all-devourer and yet remain their mouth?'"

sanskrit: cintayitvā tato vahniś cakre saṃhāram ātmanaḥ dvijānām agnihotreṣu yajñasatrakriyāsu ca
english: "Having reflected thus, Fire then withdrew himself from the agnihotras of the twice-born, from the sacrifices and from the satra rites."

sanskrit: niroṃkāravaṣaṭkārāḥ svadhāsvāhāvivarjitāḥ vināgninā prajāḥ sarvās tata āsan suduḥkhitāḥ
english: "Without the oṃkāra and the vaṣaṭkāra, bereft of the svadhā and svāhā — without Agni, all creatures were then in deep distress."

sanskrit: atharṣayaḥ samudvignā devān gatvābruvan vacaḥ agnināśāt kriyābhraṃśād bhrāntā lokās trayo 'naghāḥ vidhadhvam atra yat kāryaṃ na syāt kālātyayo yathā
english: "Then the seers, greatly agitated, went to the gods and spoke: 'O sinless ones, because of Agni's disappearance and the breakdown of rites, the three worlds are thrown into confusion — ordain what must be done here so that no time may pass in vain.'"

sanskrit: atharṣayaś ca devāś ca brahmāṇam upagamya tu agner āvedayañ śāpaṃ kriyāsaṃhāram eva ca
english: "Then the seers and the gods, approaching Brahmā, reported to him the curse upon Agni and the withdrawal of the ritual acts."

sanskrit: bhṛguṇā vai mahābhāga śapto 'gniḥ kāraṇāntare kathaṃ devamukho bhūtvā yajñabhāgāgrabhuk tathā hutabhuk sarvalokeṣu sarvabhakṣatvam eṣyati
english: "'O greatly fortunate one, Agni has been cursed by Bhṛgu for another reason — how can he, who has become the mouth of the gods, the first receiver of the share of sacrifice, the consumer of oblations in all the worlds, now become the all-devourer?'"

sanskrit: śrutvā tu tad vacas teṣām agnim āhūya lokakṛt uvāca vacanaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ bhūtabhāvanam avyayam
english: "Hearing those words of theirs, the creator of the worlds summoned Agni and spoke a gentle word to him, the eternal nurturer of all beings."

sanskrit: lokānām iha sarveṣāṃ tvaṃ kartā cānta eva ca tvaṃ dhārayasi lokāṃs trīn kriyāṇāṃ ca pravartakaḥ sa tathā kuru lokeśa nocchidyeran kriyā yathā
english: "'You are here the maker and the very end of all the worlds; you uphold the three worlds and you set the ritual acts in motion — O lord of the world, act in such a way that the rites may not be cut off.'"

sanskrit: kasmād evaṃ vimūḍhas tvam īśvaraḥ san hutāśanaḥ tvaṃ pavitraṃ yadā loke sarvabhūtagataś ca ha
english: "'Why have you become so confused, O consumer of oblations, when you are the lord? You are the purifier in the world and you pervade all beings.'"

sanskrit: na tvaṃ sarvaśarīreṇa sarvabhakṣatvam eṣyasi upādāne 'rciṣo yās te sarvaṃ dhakṣyanti tāḥ śikhin
english: "'You shall not become the all-devourer with your whole body, O blazing one — those flames of yours that take up fuel shall burn everything.'"

sanskrit: yathā sūryāṃśubhiḥ spṛṣṭaṃ sarvaṃ śuci vibhāvyate tathā tvadarcirnirdagdhaṃ sarvaṃ śuci bhaviṣyati
english: "'Just as everything touched by the rays of the sun is perceived as pure, so everything burnt by your flames shall become pure.'"

sanskrit: tad agne tvaṃ mahat tejaḥ svaprabhāvād vinirgatam svatejasaiva taṃ śāpaṃ kuru satyam ṛṣer vibho devānāṃ cātmano bhāgaṃ gṛhāṇa tvaṃ mukhe hutam
english: "'Therefore, O Agni, you are the great radiance that has issued forth from its own nature — by your own splendor fulfill the sage's curse as truth, O mighty one, and receive into your mouth the oblation that is the share of the gods and of yourself.'"
